channel.title: Happy News Company
channel.description: Real, sourced good news and good-news press releases

item.title: FDA Approves Bayer's Sunharbo, the First Factor XIa Inhibitor, to Help Prevent a Second Stroke
item.description: A once-daily pill taken with antiplatelet therapy cut ischemic stroke risk by 26% in a 12,327-person trial.

item.title: FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to First New Head and Neck Cancer Option in a Decade
item.description: Rybrevant Faspro shrank tumors in 42% of patients in a 102-person trial, though the approval is conditional on confirmatory studies.

item.title: New Jersey Warehouse Roofs Will Host 16 Community Solar Projects, Half Reserved for Lower-Income Households
item.description: Industrial property owner Faropoint plans more than 10 MW of rooftop solar that adds clean power without using any new land.

item.title: Pet Dogs Can Be Trained to Sniff Out Invasive Plants, German Study Finds
item.description: In a feasibility trial, volunteer owners and their dogs learned to detect species like Himalayan balsam with 75% average success.

item.title: 110,000 Documents on Saving Venice After the 1966 Flood to Be Digitised
item.description: On the flood's 60th anniversary, UNESCO and the Fondazione Giorgio Cini begin a two-year project to open the archive to everyone.

item.title: Newborn Deaths in Flint Halved After Cash Payments to Expecting Families, Study Finds
item.description: Michigan State researchers link the Rx Kids program to a drop in neonatal mortality, though the study is early and observational.

item.title: First Generic Version of Twice-Yearly HIV Prevention Shot Clears FDA Review
item.description: Dr. Reddy's lenacapavir, aimed at 120 lower-income countries, is expected to cost about $40 a person per year.

item.title: North Atlantic Right Whales Had 23 Calves in 2026, the Most Since 2009
item.description: NOAA data show shorter gaps between births for returning mothers, and a Florida festival this weekend celebrates the whales' return, though the species remains endangered.

item.title: Venomous Primate Feared Extinct for Nearly a Century Is Still Alive in Indonesia
item.description: A new study says the Bangka slow loris survives on Bangka Island, with rescue records pointing to a wider range than thought.

item.title: An Azores Island Switches Off Its Street Lights So Baby Seabirds Can Find the Sea
item.description: Corvo's lights-out nights help young Cory's shearwaters reach the ocean, and every resident surveyed backed the blackout.

item.title: FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to First Plasmid DNA Immunotherapy for Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis
item.description: Inovio's Voceryq gives adults with a rare, HPV-driven airway disease a new option aimed at cutting repeat surgeries.

item.title: FDA Approves Voceryq, the First Plasmid DNA Immunotherapy, for a Rare Airway Disease
item.description: Inovio's treatment for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis is cleared under accelerated approval, giving adults a new option beyond repeated surgery.

item.title: Beavers Cleared to Return to the Loch Ness Area After Roughly 500 Years
item.description: NatureScot has licensed the release of up to 15 beaver families in the River Ness catchment over three years.

item.title: Barbados Certified by WHO for Eliminating Mother-to-Child HIV Transmission
item.description: No infant infections were reported from 2022 to 2024, with 98% of pregnant women tested and 98% of those living with HIV on treatment.

item.title: More Than 25,000 Supporters Help Buy 9,500-Acre Rothbury Estate for Nature
item.description: The Wildlife Trusts completed the purchase of the Northumberland estate, with donors from over 50 countries.

item.title: Melbourne Police Officer Donates Rare Blood at All 85 Australian Lifeblood Centres
item.description: Trevor Bergman, one of about 150 Australians with the anti-D antibody, has made 545 donations in total.

item.title: Rare Arnhem Sheath-tailed Bat Recorded 400 Miles From Its Last Known Location in Northern Australia
item.description: A scientist's handheld detector picked up the elusive microbat's call during a survey at an Australian Wildlife Conservancy sanctuary.

item.title: UN Report Counts a Record 252 Million Hectares of Nature Under Restoration in 149 Countries
item.description: The first global tally of its kind finds restoration at unprecedented scale and more than a million green jobs, though funding still has to rise sharply.

item.title: Over Half of Young Adults in Diet-and-Exercise Trial Put Type 2 Diabetes Into Remission
item.description: In the RESET for Remission trial, 54% of 18-to-45-year-olds on a supervised low-calorie program reached remission at 24 weeks, versus about 4% on usual care.

item.title: Rare Short-Necked Oil Beetle Found Breeding Again at Its Only Welsh Site
item.description: After two years of finding only dead adults, surveyors have spotted larvae at Castlemartin Range in Pembrokeshire.

item.title: Green Climate Fund Approves Record $1.97 Billion at One Meeting, $3.3 Billion for 2026
item.description: Twenty-one new projects for developing countries bring this year's approvals to a new annual high, according to the fund.

item.title: Namibia's Lion Rangers Pair Smartphones With Traditional Tracking Skills to Protect Desert Lions
item.description: Local rangers across 11 conservancies have eliminated illegal lion killings in six of them, though drought-driven prey loss keeps conflict a challenge.

item.title: UCSF Immune Cells That Switch On Only in the Brain Clear Childhood Brain Tumors in Mice
item.description: Early research on a deadly pediatric cancer shows promise; human trials could begin as soon as April 2027.

item.title: Sheffield Scientist Recreates the Roman Glass That Changes Color Under Light
item.description: After 1,600 years, a University of Sheffield team has reproduced the dichroic effect of the famed Lycurgus Cup using only ingredients the Romans had.

item.title: In Punjab, Sikh and Hindu Neighbours Are Rebuilding Mosques Lost Since Partition
item.description: Villagers in Jakhiwal, Punawal and Umarpura have donated land, money, bricks and labour to restore places of worship.

item.title: Airbnb Will Send 10 Cents From Every Stay to Airbnb.org, Aiming for 1 Million Free Emergency Nights a Year
item.description: The plan targets $500 million over five years for housing people displaced by disasters and other crises.

item.title: UK Launches Low- and No-Interest Loans of Up to £35,000 for Heat Pumps, Solar Panels and Batteries
item.description: Ten lenders are offering government-backed loans for home energy upgrades, with some repayment terms stretching to 30 years.

item.title: Googly-Eyed Buoys and Bird-of-Prey Kites Cut Seabird Bycatch in Cornish Fishing Nets
item.description: A field trial with 10 Cornish fishers found kites lowered the odds of catching guillemots and razorbills by 71%, and eye-shaped buoys by 59%.

item.title: A Vitamin B5 Compound Shows Early Promise Against Psoriasis in Mice and a Small Human Trial
item.description: Researchers in Beijing traced how an immune pathway drives the skin condition, and a supplement that interrupts it helped in preliminary testing.

item.title: Netherlands Pledges Up to $500 Million to Protect Tropical Forests
item.description: The Dutch government says it will contribute to the Tropical Forest Forever Facility over ten years, a fund designed to pay countries for keeping forests standing.

item.title: London's Oxford Street Goes Car-Free, Giving Pedestrians Nearly a Kilometre of Europe's Busiest Shopping Street
item.description: Traffic is out and trees, seating and two new public squares are on the way, as the city bets on people on foot.

item.title: A Small Scottish Island's Historical Society Uncovers a Major Early Medieval Monastery
item.description: Community-funded excavations on Lismore found burials, craft workshops and evidence of gold and silver working at the site of a sixth-century monastery.

item.title: Felicia and Ben Horowitz Commit $150 Million to Nevada's First Standalone Children's Hospital
item.description: Intermountain Health says the gift is one of the largest ever made to a U.S. children's hospital and will fund specialists, programs and research in Las Vegas.

item.title: More Than $42 Million in Medical Debt Erased for Nearly 27,000 Kansans
item.description: A civic group bought the debt through the nonprofit Undue Medical Debt, and recipients are getting letters saying their old bills are paid.

item.title: New Study Suggests Van Gogh's "Starry Night" Shows a Real Sky Over Saint-Rémy in July 1889
item.description: Researchers say the painting's crescent moon, Venus and star cluster match the pre-dawn view of 22 July 1889.

item.title: Three Michigan Tribes Are Working to Bring Back a Fish Missing for Nearly a Century
item.description: Young Arctic grayling and hundreds of thousands of eggs have been released, though success will take years to judge.

item.title: Kenya Launches $160 Million Thamani Asili Plan to Fund Conservation for the Next Decade
item.description: The Nature Conservancy and Enduring Earth are backing a community-led effort that aims to reach roughly 17 million hectares.

item.title: Orphaned Walrus Calf Found Between Two Carcasses in Alaska Gets a New Home in Florida
item.description: A student researcher spotted the calf's stomach move; weeks later, five-month-old Annautaq is settling in at SeaWorld Orlando.

item.title: [Press Release] Squamish Sauna Hat Shop Is Giving Away Free Wool Sauna Hats This Christmas
item.description: Sauna Hats Canada will send a grey wool bucket sauna hat to anyone in Canada who joins its list. Customers pay only the shipping.

item.title: [Press Release] Squamish Photographer Opens Library of Sea to Sky Stock Photos, Licensed Directly With No Subscription
item.description: Jeremy Allen of The Full Time Hobby has put hundreds of photos of Squamish, Whistler and British Columbia online for businesses to license direct from the photographer.
